help_articles.title: What is SME Hub?
help_articles.summary: A free community for Canadian small-business owners, from the team behind CanadianSME Small Business Magazine.
help_articles.html:
SME Hub is an online community where Canadian small-business owners connect, ask questions, share what works and find customers through recommendations and warm introductions.

It is run by CanadianSME, the team behind CanadianSME Small Business Magazine, which has covered Canadian small business since 2018.

What you can do on SME Hub

  • Build a profile for you and a page for your business.
  • Ask questions and share wins, jobs and introductions in the feed.
  • Join groups on topics like money, marketing, hiring, exporting and AI.
  • Find and message other owners, advisors and Canadian suppliers.
  • Get recommended by people you have worked with, and ask for introductions through people you both know.
  • List your business in the Canada-wide Business Directory.
  • Use AI to answer business questions and suggest who to meet.
TipSME Hub is free to join. Paid plans add things like offers, private groups and more AI. See Free, Plus and Advisor plans compared.

help_articles.title: Create your account
help_articles.summary: Join free in about two minutes. No card needed.
help_articles.tags: join sign up register new account password code
help_articles.html:
1. Go to SME Hub and select Join free (or Join now at the top of any page).
  2. Sign up with Google or LinkedIn, or fill in your first and last name, your business name and your work email. No business yet? Write "Starting soon".
  3. Add your business website or Google listing if you have one. It’s optional, and it lets AI set up your profile for you.
  4. Create a password. The checklist turns green as you meet each rule: 8 or more characters, at least one number, upper and lower case or a symbol, and not a common password.
  5. Choose your province or territory and agree to the Terms. Ticking the newsletter box is up to you.
  6. Select Create my free account.
  7. We email you a 6-digit code. Type or paste it and select Confirm my email. The code works for 60 minutes. Didn’t get it? Check your spam folder, or select Send a new code.
  8. AI sets up your profile. If you added your website, it drafts your profile and business page from it. No website? Answer 3 quick questions instead. Check the draft, change anything you like, then select Looks good, save. See Get your profile ready.
Good to knowUse your real name and your real business. Profiles that pretend to be someone else are removed. See Community guidelines.

help_articles.title: Get your profile ready
help_articles.summary: Five quick things that help the right people find you, and how AI can do most of them for you.
help_articles.tags: onboarding checklist new member ready profile complete photo headline business page website ai setup
help_articles.html:
Your profile is ready when it has all 5 of these:

  1. A profile photo. Owners reply to people they can see.
  2. A headline. Your role and business, for example "Owner, Morgan Home Renovations".
  3. Your city. So owners near you can find you. Only your city shows, never your address.
  4. What you can help with. Short tags. They decide who finds you in search.
  5. A business page. Puts your business in the Business Directory.

Until your profile is ready, a Your profile is N of 5 ready card sits at the top of your Home page and your profile. Each step has its own button.

Let AI do it for you

Select Set it up for me on the card, then paste your business website or Google Business Profile link. AI reads it and drafts your headline, city, introduction, "Can help with" tags and business page. You check everything and change anything before you save.

No website? Select No website? Answer 3 questions: your role and business, your city, and what you can help with.

What a ready profile gets you

Until your profile has…You can’t…
A photo and a headlineSend connection requests or ask for introductions. We ask you to add them first, in the same window.
A business pageAppear in the Business Directory
All 5Appear in member search, daily "People to meet" and AI matchmaking for other members

You can always read posts, join groups, ask questions and message people who contact you.

TipA ready profile also lets you apply for the Get featured: the Member Spotlight in CanadianSME Small Business Magazine.

Reminder emails

If your profile isn’t ready, we send up to 3 short emails in your first 2 weeks, each about one missing step. They stop as soon as your profile is ready. You can turn them off in Email notifications.

help_articles.title: Profile types and badges
help_articles.summary: Business owner, SME Advisor, maker, service provider: what each label means.
help_articles.html:
Your profile type tells members what kind of member you are. It shows as a tag on your profile and member card, and it helps people filter the directory.

  • Business owner: you run a small business.
  • SME Advisor: an expert who serves small businesses, such as an accountant, lawyer, consultant or coach. Comes with the Advisor plan. See Become an SME Advisor.
  • Maker: you make products in Canada.
  • Service provider: a company that sells services or software to small businesses.

Badges

  • Founding Member: one of the first 500 members. See The Founding Member badge.
  • SME Advisor: shown on your profile and your posts.
  • Recommended by N: how many members have recommended you. See Recommendations: give and ask.

help_articles.title: Recommendations: give and ask
help_articles.summary: Vouch for people you have worked with, and ask clients and partners to vouch for you.
help_articles.html:
Recommendations are short notes from members you have worked with. They show on your profile, and your profile header shows Recommended by N.

Write a recommendation

  1. Open the member’s profile.
  2. Select Recommend followed by their name.
  3. Choose how you know them, for example Client or Referral partner.
  4. Write one or two honest sentences about working with them.
  5. Select Send for approval. It appears on their profile once they approve it.

Approve recommendations you receive

New recommendations wait in your Recommendations section under Waiting for your approval. Select Show on my profile or Do not show.

Ask for a recommendation

  1. Open your own profile and go to Recommendations.
  2. Select Ask for a recommendation.
  3. Choose the people to ask, add a short note and select Send.
TipSpecific beats general: "Rebuilt our office in three weeks and stayed on budget" helps more than "Great to work with".

help_articles.title: Get featured: the Member Spotlight
help_articles.summary: Apply to be featured in CanadianSME Small Business Magazine.
help_articles.tags: spotlight featured magazine press feature canadiansme
help_articles.html:
Every month, CanadianSME Small Business Magazine and its newsletter feature SME Hub members and their businesses. It’s free.

Who can apply

Any member whose profile is ready: photo, headline, city, "Can help with" and a business page. See Get your profile ready.

How to apply

  1. Open Explore, then Member Spotlight. Once your profile is ready, you’ll also see an Apply button at the top of your profile.
  2. Answer 3 short questions: what your business does, one win or lesson, and what you’d like readers to know.
  3. Tick the box so CanadianSME can use your photo, business name and answers.
  4. Select Apply for the Spotlight.

What happens next

The CanadianSME editorial team picks members each month. If you’re chosen, we email you with the issue, your editor and what they need. Chosen members get a feature in the magazine, a mention in the newsletter, a social media post and a Spotlight badge on their profile for 30 days.

help_articles.title: Connect or follow: what is the difference?
help_articles.summary: Connections are two-way. Following is one-way.
help_articles.html:
• Connect: you send a request and the other member accepts. You both see each other’s updates, you can share with "Connections only", and you can introduce each other to people.
  • Follow: you see someone’s public posts in your feed. They don’t need to accept.

When you connect with someone, you also follow them automatically.

Good to knowYou need a profile photo and a headline before you can send connection requests. If either is missing, SME Hub asks you to add them first, in the same window. See Get your profile ready.

Send a connection request

  1. Select + Connect on a member’s profile, card or post.
  2. The button changes to Request sent until they reply.

help_articles.title: Ask for a warm introduction
help_articles.summary: Meet someone through a connection you both share.
help_articles.html:
A warm introduction is when someone you both know introduces you. It is the fastest way to get a reply.

  1. Open the profile of the person you want to meet.
  2. Look for mutual connections.
  3. Select Ask for an introduction.
  4. Under Who should introduce you?, choose the mutual connection to ask.
  5. Write a short note saying why you want to meet, then select Send request.
  6. Your connection decides whether to make the introduction. You’ll get a message either way.
TipExplain what’s in it for the other person, for example "I’m looking for a bakery to supply our café events".

help_articles.summary: Stop someone contacting you and hide their content.
help_articles.html:
1. Open the member’s profile, or the menu on one of their posts.

When you block someone:

  • They can’t message you or send you a connection request.
  • They are not told that you blocked them.

To undo, go to Me, then Blocked members, and select Unblock. See also Report a post, member, business or review.

help_articles.summary: Add a title, photo, poll, hashtags or a group, or schedule it for later.

  2. Choose a post type. See Post types: Question, Win, Offer, Hiring, Intro.

    • Schedule: choose a date and time to publish later.

help_articles.summary: Find a Canadian small business for sale and contact the seller.
help_articles.tags: buy business for sale acquisition purchase seller confidential owner earnings
help_articles.html:
Businesses for sale lists Canadian small businesses looking for a new owner. Every listing comes from a paid SME Hub member, and there is no broker in the middle.

Find a business

  1. Open Explore, then Businesses for Sale. You can also select Businesses for sale on the Business Directory page.
  2. Search by type of business, keyword or city, and pick a province.
  3. Narrow the list by industry, asking price or type of sale.

Anyone can see the headline, area, industry and asking price. Signed-in members also see yearly sales, owner earnings, what’s included, why the owner is selling and who the seller is. Joining is free.

TipOwner earnings is what the business earns for one full-time owner each year, before the owner’s pay, interest and tax. Ask the seller how they worked it out.

Types of sale

TypeWhat it means
Full saleYou buy the whole business.
Partner wanted (part stake)The owner sells part of the business and stays on.
Assets onlyYou buy equipment, stock or the brand, but not the running business.

Contact the seller

  1. Open the listing and select Contact the seller.
  2. Say how you’ll pay and when you want to buy, then write a short message about yourself.
  3. Tick the box to agree to keep the seller’s details private.
  4. Select Send to the seller. They reply in your messages.

Some sellers stay confidential. You’ll see Confidential seller until they choose to share their name and documents with you.

Save a listing

Select the bookmark on any listing to save it. Your saved listings are on the Saved tab. We email you if the price changes or the business goes under offer.

Buy safely

  • Ask an accountant to check the financial statements.
  • Use a lawyer for the offer and purchase agreement.
  • Never send money to hold a business. SME Hub never asks for payment.
  • If something looks wrong, select Report this listing. The seller won’t know who reported it.

A shield and Checked by the Hub team means our team has checked that the seller is a real paid member and the listing follows our rules. It doesn’t mean we’ve checked the business’s accounts.

help_articles.title: Sell your business on SME Hub
help_articles.summary: List your business for sale, stay confidential and handle buyer enquiries.
help_articles.tags: sell business for sale listing exit retire confidential enquiries buyers
help_articles.html:
PlansListing a business for sale is included with the Plus and Advisor plans. Browsing and contacting sellers is free for every member. See Free, Plus and Advisor plans compared.

List your business

  1. Open Explore, then Businesses for Sale, and select Sell your business.
  2. Fill in the 5 short sections: the basics, price and numbers, about the business, what’s included, and photo and privacy. It takes about 10 minutes.
  3. Check the preview on the right, then select Publish listing.

Your listing goes live straight away. The Hub team checks every new listing within 2 working days. Once it’s checked, buyers see a shield on it.

TipListings with an asking price get far more enquiries than Price on request. Talk to an accountant about the value before you list.

Stay confidential

Keep my name and business name hidden is on by default. Buyers see Confidential seller and only the area you choose, such as a neighbourhood or region. Leave your business name out of the headline and avoid photos of your shop sign.

You decide who learns more. When you select Share documents and my name on an enquiry, only that buyer sees your name and documents.

Handle enquiries

Open My listings to see views, saves and enquiries for each listing. Each enquiry shows how the buyer will pay, when they want to buy and their message.

  • Reply opens a chat with the buyer.
  • Share documents and my name shares your documents with that buyer only.

We also email you each time a buyer gets in touch.

Update your listing

On My listings you can:

help_articles.summary: How the Hub team reviews reports.
help_articles.html:
• Every report goes to the Hub moderation team.

  • You get a notification when there is a decision on something you reported.

help_articles.title: Log in, and the code on new devices
help_articles.summary: How logging in works, and why we sometimes email you a code.
help_articles.tags: login log in sign in code two-step new device locked
help_articles.html:
1. Select Sign in at the top of any page.
  2. Enter your email and password, or use Google or LinkedIn if that is how you joined.
  3. Leave Keep me logged in on this device ticked on your own computer or phone. Untick it on a shared computer.

The 6-digit code on a new device

When you log in from a computer, phone or browser we haven’t seen before, we email you a 6-digit code to make sure it’s really you. Enter it to finish logging in. The code works for 10 minutes. Tick Trust this device for 30 days so we don’t ask again on that device.

We also email you about every sign-in from a new device. If it wasn’t you, change your password straight away. See Change your password and see where you’re logged in.

Too many tries

After 5 wrong passwords in a row, we pause sign-ins to your account for 15 minutes and email you. Wait, or reset your password. See Forgot your password? Reset it.

help_articles.title: Close your account
help_articles.summary: Remove your profile, with 30 days to change your mind.
help_articles.html:
1. Go to Me, then Privacy and account.
  2. Under Close my account, follow the steps.

If you have a paid plan, cancel it first. See Upgrade, change or cancel your plan. Closing your account removes your profile and your posts. Business pages you own should be handed to another team member first.

Changed your mind?

You have 30 days to restore your account. Use the Restore my account link in the email we send you, or just log in again. After 30 days your information is permanently deleted and we email you to confirm.
